content: 1. Administer 200 mg of the medication orally four times daily, ideally 30 minutes before meals. If symptom control is not achieved within 2-3 weeks, the dose may be increased to a maximum of 40 mg/kg/day. 2. For patients over 12 years of age, the initial dose is 200 mg orally four times daily, 30 minutes prior to meals. If the therapeutic effect is unsatisfactory after 2-3 weeks, the dose may be doubled, but it should not exceed 400 mg orally four times daily. 3. For children aged 2-12 years, the recommended dose is 100 mg orally four times daily, administered 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. The dose may be doubled if symptom control is inadequate after 2-3 weeks, but it should not exceed 40 mg/kg/day. 4. For children under 2 years of age, the safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established, and its use is not recommended. 5. For systemic mastocytosis, administer the medication 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. 6. For food allergies and inflammatory bowel disease, administer the medication 15-20 minutes before meals. 7. To prepare the solution, dilute the contents of the ampule in a glass of plain water and stir well. Do not mix with fruit juice, soda, milk, or any other fluid. Consume the solution immediately after preparation and do not prepare it in advance. 8. This medication is not effective immediately. Regular use is required to achieve the desired therapeutic effect, which may take 2-3 weeks. 9. This medication is for oral use only and should not be used for inhalation, nasal administration, or injection. 10. Common side effects include headache, muscle aches, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, and rash. Rare but serious side effects include severe anaphylactic reactions, pancytopenia, and psychosis. 11. The medication is excreted through both biliary and renal routes. Patients with hepatic or renal insufficiency should be closely monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 12. Use caution in patients with a history of cardiac arrhythmias or hepatic/renal impairment. 13. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly needed (Pregnancy Category B). It is unknown if the drug is excreted in breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. 14. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of side effects. Maintain a list of all medications and supplements being taken and share it with your healthcare provider. 15. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. For U.S. residents, call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. 16. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. 17. Store the ampules in their foil pouches at room temperature, away from heat and light. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. 18. Symptoms may recur when tapering or discontinuing the medication, so caution is advised during withdrawal. 19. This medication is not beneficial in acute settings and is intended for long-term management. 20. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
